title: Pay now, terms later and rolling formation
summary: The cases disagree about whether later-delivered terms define the initial offer or propose additions to an existing contract.
notes: Hill uses retention after a review-and-return period to complete the vendor’s offer and treats the one-form transaction outside § 2-207. Klocek finds no textual two-form prerequisite and, on its evidentiary record, assumes the consumer made the offer and the vendor accepted earlier. The differences include governing law, procedural posture, notice, and offeror identity as well as the length of the return period. The notes retain later developments as dated reports.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 294–304. Open assigned page 294.
